messages:
Anya: Heads up — after the model v3.7 onboard this morning, canary p95 latency jumped ~2.2x and throughput dropped ~30% on the serving pool. Noted mostly for short-chat workloads.
Ben: ugh. Any obvious changes in kernel selection or batch distribution?
Anya: Noted tokenizer changed from byte-level to merged-vocab in the checkpoint; average tokenization length dropped ~18% which shifted batching windows. Kernel selector logs show a different kernel chosen for many requests.
Marco: dropping logs from the kernel selector probe:
```
KERNEL_SELECTOR: req_id=abcd1234 model=v3.7 seq_len=48 chosen_kernel=fast_attn_v2 batch_size=1 reason=latency_estimate
KERNEL_SELECTOR: req_id=efgh5678 model=v3.7 seq_len=12 chosen_kernel=kv_prefetch_v1 batch_size=8 reason=throughput_estimate
```
Notice the selector is favoring low-batch, low-latency kernels for sequences that used to bin into mid-batch.
Ben: that explains throughput. Could be the heuristic threshold uses absolute seq_len not percentiles. Did CI perf catch this?
ci-bot: perf-ci: model_onboard_integration v3.7 — p95 latency regression detected (+120%) — blocking: true — job: perf-canary-22
Sara: We should pause rollout and revert the canary until we have a mitigation. Reverting will buy time for a proper fix.
Anya: +1 on pause. But I want to bisect whether the tokenizer artifact or the kernel-selector heuristic introduced the delta. Proposing: shadow older tokenizer on a subset and run same load.
Marco: quick repro command (can run in staging):
```
wrk -t12 -c200 -d60s http://staging-v3.7/generate -H "Content-Type: application/json" -p small_chat.json
# small_chat.json contains 90% prompts length ~10 tokens
```
ops-bot: canary metrics snapshot: {"kv_cache_evictions_per_min": 78, "prefetch_misses": 42, "avg_batch_size": 3.1} vs baseline {"kv_cache_evictions_per_min": 11, "avg_batch_size": 5.2} 
Ben: KV evictions spiking — maybe kernel change increased per-request memory or changed KV key distribution. If batch sizes shrink, more warmups, leading to eviction churn.
Anya: I ran a targeted profile: allocation hotspot in kernel fast_attn_v2 for short sequences — memory working set up by ~30%. Profiling snippet:
```
alloc_profile:
  fast_attn_v2: rss +120MB peaks on warmup
  kv_prefetch_v1: rss +30MB
```
Marco: candidate fixes: 1) adjust kernel selector thresholds to consider relative seq_len distribution (percentile-aware), 2) fall back to kv_prefetch_v1 for seq_len <= 16, 3) tweak tokenizer to preserve more tokens (ugh).
Sara: For immediate action: pause canary rollout, revert v3.7 in canary, and push a config change to selector to force previous kernel mapping. Then open a follow-up to design percentile-aware selector.
Anya: Agreed. I'll submit a quick revert PR and a selector override flag. PR: r/1234 (revert canary).
Ben: I'll run the bisect on the selector heuristic — range: commits between kernel-selector@main~20..kernel-selector@main (today) — will post a bisection log shortly.
ci-bot: perf-ci: started bisect job perf-bisect-789 (tracking in jobs/perf-bisect-789)
Marco: logging note: if you run local repro, set env KERNEL_SELECTOR_DEBUG=1 and collect /tmp/ks-*.log for correlation.
Anya: Thanks, all. Action items: pause canary (Sara), revert PR (Anya), bisect heuristic (Ben), run shadow tokenizer test (Marco). Will update thread when we have data. :thumbsup:
Ben: preliminary bisect result: commit 14d2a5 bumped heuristic threshold from 0.6->0.8 for short_seq branch. Reverting that locally reduces p95 by ~45% in staging.
Anya: Nice find — that commit came in with a perf micro-optimization but had unexpected side effects with the new tokenizer distribution. We'll roll back the threshold and add percentile weighting to avoid future regressions.
Sara: rolling back canary now. Notifying infra for rollback window 10:30-11:00.
ops-bot: rollback started for canary pool (id cp-019), estimated time 6m.
Anya: Follow-up: open ticket PERF-462 to make selector percentiles, and PERF-463 to add CI gating for model-onboard tokenizer distribution diffs.
Marco: also adding a small e2e test: token length histogram compare >=95% match before allowing rollout.
Anya: closing loop — will post post-mortem link once done.
